docs(acp-feedback): report environment-dependent permission requests (#49)

A user hit the case our own probe had only seen from one side: grok sends
zero session/request_permission for an in-workspace edit on some Windows 11
hosts, while the same build and settings prompt reliably on macOS and a Win 11
Azure VM. It's invariant under permission_mode, yolo, support_permission and a
pristine default config, so a client cannot explain it or work around it --
our inline diff restores review, but nothing client-side can restore approval.

This was already noted internally in research/edit-diff.md; it belongs upstream,
where it's actionable. The user report is stronger evidence than the probe alone.

Allow read-only command chains in plan mode (#36)

The gate's metachar regex treated any '&' or ';' as instant rejection, so a
harmless 'cd repo && git status' was blocked — which crashed grok-4.5's
planning phase (tool_error -> no plan.md). Sequencing operators (&&, ||, ;, |)
now split the command and every segment must independently pass the read-only
allowlist; redirects, substitution, script blocks, and lone-& backgrounding
still block outright, and an operator hidden inside quotes mis-splits into
segments that fail the allowlist, so mis-parses err toward blocking.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Land the caret in the input on session swaps too

New session, a history-row re-focus, and a disk restore all funnel through
resetForNewSession (the host's clearMessages) — focus the input there so the
caret is ready after every swap, not just panel open/window refocus. Guarded
on document.hasFocus(): user-initiated swaps start with a click inside the
webview, but a host-initiated clear (an automatic restart) can arrive while
the user is typing in the editor, and focusing then would yank keyboard focus
across panels.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Confirm /compact on screen: live-only 'Compacted.' in the turn's bubble

A native compact streams no agent content, so the turn ended with an empty
bubble and no sign it worked (the donut's 0 is easy to miss). Emit a
messageChunk when the compact prompt resolves — it rides the session buffer
(survives re-focus) but isn't in grok's history, so a disk restore doesn't

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tell grok not to Read inline images from disk (tag-line hint)

First Windows dogfood of the vision feature: the CLI persists an incoming
image block to its own sessions/<id>/assets/*.png and surfaces that path in
the model's context, so the model Read-attempted the binary and failed
('Cannot read binary file') on a pasted image whose pixels it already had —
harmless but a red noise row on every paste. The [Image #N] tag parenthetical
now carries a do-not-Read hint (pasted and disk-import variants);
parseImageTags peels it back off so restore still sees a clean origin path.
Point-of-use beats a primer rule: primer additions have blast radius (v3->v4
history) and fade over long contexts; the tag rides exactly the turns that
tempt the model.

Release v1.4.30

Fix the pre-PR review findings: attachment races + parenthesized image paths

Three race windows and one asymmetry, from the adversarial review pass
over the vision-input range:

- Message ordering only guarantees an attachment op posted before send
  STARTED handling — its fs awaits could still be mid-flight when
  handleSend snapshotted chips (VS Code doesn't serialize async
  onDidReceiveMessage handlers), so a fast paste-then-Enter could send
  without its image. handleSend now settles the in-flight staging set
  (trackAttach/pendingAttach) before snapshotting.
- The post-send clear was wholesale (filter to implicit-only), wiping
  any chip staged while images were pre-reading. The pure consumeChips
  (chips.ts) drops exactly the snapshotted ids instead — late arrivals
  ride the next turn.
- parseImageTags' [^)]* stopped at the FIRST `)`, so a browser-dedup
  filename — `screenshot (1).png` — failed the whole tag line on
  restore and leaked into the body as literal text. Greedy + $-anchored
  now, so the close lands on the LAST paren.
- The image pre-read loop gen-checked its failure path but not success:
  a client torn down during the reads could still consume chips and
  unlink staged files for a prompt that never went out. Mirror the guard.

Test floor 703 -> 707.

Unify the composer into one card; style the webview scrollbars

The composer read as three stacked strips — attachments row above, a
bordered textarea, and a naked toolbar below — split further by the
composer's full-width border-top. All three now live inside a single

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix /compact: slash commands must lead the text block, and the donut must accept 0

Two root causes behind "compact didn't do anything". First, buildPrompt put
the <vscode-context> envelope BEFORE the user text, and the CLI only
dispatches a slash command at position 0 of the text block — so with the
implicit active-editor chip present, every typed /compact silently degraded
into an ordinary LLM turn that *grew* context 6x. Second, even a dispatched
compact reports totalTokens: 0 (the "context reset" marker), which chat.js's
truthy check swallowed, freezing the donut at the pre-compact value.

- matchSlashCommand (slash-filter) gates the send path: token shape validated
  against the CLI's advertised availableCommands (shape-only before the list
  arrives — a wrongly-trailed context costs more than a wrongly-led one)
- buildPrompt/buildPromptWithImages flip to text-first for a confirmed
  command; the CLI tolerates trailing context (probe variants C/D)
- promptComplete lets totalTokens 0 through (!= null, not truthy)
- re-prime after a confirmed /compact: the native history rewrite can fold
  the hidden plan-protocol primer away, same distrust as the restore path

Wire evidence + async-rewrite findings in research/compact.md; the
four-variant probe is research/compact-probe.cjs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show the selected line range on sent-message chips, live and on restore

The composer chip gained a live selection range last commit, but the
range vanished the moment you hit send: the bubble chip rendered only a
(20-char-truncated) basename, and a restored session showed the selection
as a raw fenced code block pasted into your own bubble. Now both ends
match the composer: `prompt-builder.ts:60-82` (single line `a.ts:8`),
full range on the tooltip, JS truncation replaced by CSS ellipsis
(.msg-chip span needs its own nowrap — unlike .chip it inherits none).

Restore rides a new pure parser, parseSelectionBlocks: it peels
buildPrompt's leading fenced selection snippets back into ranged chips,
chained between the envelope and image-tag parsers so each strips exactly
its own layer of the wire. Only complete blocks anchored at the start of
the body are taken — a half-streamed block (replay re-parses per chunk)
and a selection-shaped block amid the user's own words stay put; selected
code containing a bare ``` is ambiguous on the wire (buildPrompt does no
fence escaping), so we stop at the first standalone closing fence exactly
as markdown would. The stripped body also becomes the restored bubble's
_copyText, fixing copy-on-restored-message yielding "" instead of the
user's words.

Tests 677 -> 688: parser round-trips driven by real buildPrompt /
buildPromptWithImages output (locking wire sync), live + restore DOM
chips, single-line ranges, streaming safety, and the full three-parser
chain over a combined envelope + selection + image prompt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Mirror the live editor selection on the context chip; drop the 10-char cut

The composer's active-editor chip was a static snapshot: renderChips hard-cut
the file name to 10 chars ("vitest.per…"), and nothing subscribed to
onDidChangeTextEditorSelection, so selecting lines in the editor never showed
on the chip or reached the prompt. Claude Code's context chip is the model:
full name, live `:8-15` line-range suffix, selection content sent along.

- One refreshImplicitChip path now serves init, editor switch, selection
  change, config flip, and post-send — the old addActiveEditorChip silently
  desynced host and webview when the editor went away (cleared host-side,
  never posted). No-op diffing keeps caret movement at zero postMessage
  traffic: the chip only stores the line pair, and an empty selection
  normalizes to the previous empty one.
- The prompt layer needed zero changes: buildPrompt already renders any chip
  with a selection range as a fenced snippet, so the implicit chip upgrades
  from the ambient "Currently open" path line to real selected content.
- The chip now survives a send (it mirrors IDE state, not a one-shot
  attachment) by passing through the post-send clear — which is also what
  preserves the user's eye-off choice (review-caught: rebuilding from scratch
  resurfaced context the user had explicitly hidden).
- grok.includeActiveFileByDefault applies immediately on toggle instead of on
  the next editor switch.
- Full file name rides the DOM (escaped — the old innerHTML interpolation
  didn't escape); pathological lengths ellipsize via CSS at 220px.

Tests 671 → 677 (implicit-chip selection identity, implicit+selection fenced
prompt, DOM label/range/single-line/escape).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Harden vision input: fix the 16 review findings on e5e5eee

The root problems were lifecycle and silence. Pasted images lived in
grok's session dir, which the empty-session cleanup deletes — a pending
screenshot died when you switched sessions. They now stage in
session-neutral globalStorage (<globalStorage>/image-staging/), are
pre-read + validated only at send, and any unreadable image blocks the
whole send with chips intact: probe-verified that a silently dropped
attachment leaves a dangling [Image #N] tag that sends the model hunting
the workspace for a file that never arrived.

Design calls, probe-driven (research/vision-probe.cjs, grok 0.2.87):
- No capability gate: the CLI still advertises
  promptCapabilities.image:false but accepts the blocks — behavior over
  advertisement, pinned by the new vision-prompt live test so a build
  that starts rejecting image blocks fails the release gate.
- SVG stays a path chip (an attached SVG is source the user wants grok
  to read/edit); raster whitelist png/jpe?g/gif/webp at the documented
  20MiB cap, oversized/unsupported files fall back to path chips.
- Text keeps position 0 with [Image #N] tags trailing — a leading tag
  broke /command dispatch; disk imports carry the origin path in the tag
  so grok can act on the real file, not just the pixels.
- send no longer round-trips chips through the webview (host-owned):
  closes the arbitrary-path-read trust edge and the paste→Enter race in
  one move; /compact sends bare without clearing composer attachments.
- [Image #N] numbering is session-scoped (Session.imageCounter,
  re-seeded from replayed prompts on restore); parseImageTags strips
  only our own leading/trailing tag shapes so a literal tag in the
  middle of the user's words survives restore.

Tests 640 → 671 (chips whitelist, prompt-builder byte-equivalence,
parseImageTags round-trips, DOM paste suite, fake-CLI vision echo);
live --quick 6/6 incl. vision-prompt against real grok.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add image paste and upload via ACP vision blocks

Path-only file chips made grok call fs/read_text_file on PNGs and fail.
Mirror the CLI TUI: save pasted/uploaded images under the session images/
dir, tag prompts with [Image #N], and send inline base64 image blocks so
the model can actually see screenshots from Ctrl+V and the + picker.

Fix #30: recover the edit diff on session restore, not just live

The first #30 fix kept a lone edit's tool group expandable, but on
session/load the diff still vanished — the reported symptom. Root cause:
grok delivers the structured `content:[{type:"diff"}]` block on DIFFERENT
messages by path. LIVE it rides a follow-up tool_call_update (the tool_call
is a bare "StrReplace" with no content); on REPLAY the whole edit collapses
into one completed tool_call that carries the diff itself, with no separate
update. chat.js only extracted diffs from tool_call_update, so a restored
edit kept its expandable group but had nothing to open.

Extract diffs from both message kinds (shared applyToolDiffs). The original
DOM test assumed the wrong replay shape (diff on a separate update) so it
passed green while restore was broken; rewrite it to grok's real reload wire,
and add a real-grok `edit-diff-restore` live test that drives an actual edit
through session/load — the only layer that can catch this wire drift.

Verified against grok 0.2.82 with a capture probe (live vs replay) and the
new live test: diff present live (tool_call_update) and on restore (tool_call).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix #30: keep a standalone edit expandable so its diff stays reviewable

A permission that resolved to a single edit collapsed to a bare `.tool-flat`
row (icon + label, no chevron, no body), discarding the diff preview that
attachDiffPreviewToToolItem appends to the tool-item in the body — so the edit
could not be expanded to review the change. A read+edit batch stayed an
expandable `.tool-group`, so its diff survived; that was the reported contrast.
On restore it was worse: renderRestoredPermissionForTool closes the group
before the tool_call_update carrying the diff arrives, orphaning the preview.

closeToolGroup no longer flattens a lone edit/write — it keeps the group
(chevron + body) so the diff lands and stays reachable in both the live and
replay orderings. Non-edit single tools still flatten as before.

Release v1.4.13 — reactive auto-downgrade + retry for future broken Grok CLI builds (#22)

Document #22 stdio-EOF regression is macOS-clean; add mac probe

Verified on macOS (Apple Silicon) that grok 0.2.64 — the build that hangs on
Windows — answers the stdin-open ACP initialize handshake in ~450ms (4/4 runs),
so the regression is Windows-only and the existing win32 gate on the auto-pin is
correct. Follow-up sent to xAI via /feedback.

Auto-pin broken Grok CLI 0.2.61–0.2.64 + block unsupported updates (#22) (v1.4.12)

Grok CLI 0.2.61–0.2.64 regressed `agent stdio`: the agent stops reading
stdin until EOF, so the ACP `initialize` handshake never completes for a
live client and sessions can't start ("exited code null" / "initialize timed
out"). The extension can't make the CLI read stdin, so it now detects the
broken version range on startup and pins the CLI back to the last working
build (0.2.60), and refuses to update onto an unsupported build (the menu
action is disabled with a note; below 0.2.60 it updates to 0.2.60, never
latest). Full diagnosis + xAI bug report in research/stdio-eof-regression.md.

Lets users zoom the Grok chat panel on its own — text, icons, and
spacing together — without rescaling the rest of VS Code (the reporter's
complaint in #14 about the global Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+=). It's a percent
setting (60–300, default 100) at User or Workspace scope and applies
live with no reload.

The webview uses CSS `zoom`, which scales layout but which `vh` units
ignore — a 100vh body at zoom 0.7 renders at 70vh and leaves dead space
below the composer. Both the `zoom` and a `height: calc(100vh /
var(--chat-zoom))` compensation are derived from one `--chat-zoom`
variable (baked into <body> by the host, updated live via postMessage),
so the composer stays pinned to the bottom at any scale.

Also: README screenshots for Voice input and the Agent Dashboard, plus a
few wire-level details moved from the feature blurbs into
docs/architecture.md.

473 tests green; live gate green (5 passed, image-gen SKIP).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Multi-session Agent Dashboard + eager non-blocking primer (v1.4.8)

Keeps a pool of live grok sessions instead of one — instant lossless
re-focus (each session buffers its webview posts, so focusing replays
the buffer with no grok reload or kill), status dots in the history
dropdown (a derived, persisted unread badge that survives idle reaping
and a VS Code restart), and silent idle-TTL + LRU reaping that never
touches the focused or a working/needs-you session.

Also fixes the pre-turn primer latency. The hidden plan-mode primer now
fires eagerly + non-blocking the moment a session goes live (new,
restore, post-/compact) instead of in front of the user's first prompt.
The first real send awaits the same in-flight primer turn and is
released the instant it acks; the user's bubble shows immediately with a
"Grokking…" indicator standing in until grok produces content. The
primer was trimmed to v4 — the product-blurb paragraph + repo URL that
tempted agentic grok into a 15–40s pre-turn workspace exploration are
gone, replaced by an explicit do-not-act / "reply with just ok"
constraint. The plan-verdict protocol itself is unchanged.

Render math with MathJax + export equations/diagrams as PNG/SVG (v1.4.7)

Replaces KaTeX with vendored MathJax (tex-svg-full), so every equation is
a self-contained SVG — closer to real LaTeX, and exportable. Driving it
via tex2svg+outerHTML skips MathJax's injected stylesheet, so we disable

Adds a Copy/Download/Open hover overlay to display math and rendered
mermaid (both are SVG now). Download quick-picks PNG (WYSIWYG, theme

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

live-tests: video-gen timeout is an inconclusive SKIP, not a FAIL

The 10-min bump from the previous commit didn't help — /imagine-video
timed out at 10 min just like 5. A 2-min diagnostic run showed why: in
this bare headless harness grok 0.2.x doesn't cleanly generate one clip,
it spins (3474 updates, Glob/Grep, 12 media-gen tool calls with
status:failed) and never finishes, regardless of the wait. The feature
works interactively — this is a harness artifact, not a regression.

So a timeout is now reported as SKIP (doesn't fail the gate), with a
diagnostic of what grok was last doing so a genuine hang (no tool calls)
still stands out. Reverted the wait to the original 5 min since waiting
longer only delays the inevitable SKIP.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

live-tests: wait 10 min for video-gen (real /imagine-video exceeds 5 min)

The video-gen gate FAILed on a 300s timeout two releases running, but

Render Mermaid diagrams via vendored Mermaid (v1.4.6)

Grok answers with ```mermaid fences that the markdown renderer showed

  the whole integration suite exercises this, and the live suite reports the
  echo count (live-echo×N) to watch for future drift.

- Subagent card never fired on the native build: grok 0.2.x has no
  spawn_subagent tool — it delegates via a backgrounded run_terminal_command.
  isSubagentToolCall now cards that (is_background / [bg] title), still excludes
  the get_command_or_subagent_output poller, and leaves foreground commands in
  the tool group. Confirmed live: real grok delegated and the cards fired.

Silently update grok CLI on extension upgrade; fix welcome status lifecycle

grok doesn't auto-update, so installing a newer extension could leave the
user on a stale CLI whose wire format the new extension no longer matches.
Now the first session start after the extension's own version changes runs
`grok update` once before spawning the CLI, so the next handshake reports the
updated version. Gated on a real upgrade (never a fresh install), once per
activation, via execFile while no grok process is alive (Windows binary lock),
best-effort. The gate is the pure, unit-tested extensionWasUpgraded.

The welcome status line was flipping to "connected" at the ACP handshake,
before the hidden primer turn had been sent and processed and while the
composer spinner was still up — claiming readiness too early. It now follows
the real lifecycle: "Updating Grok Build CLI…" -> "starting…" (held through
priming) -> "connected · v<version>" only when the spinner clears.

Add on-demand real-grok pre-release suite + document the three test layers

The grok-free unit/DOM/integration suite (npm test) can only prove our protocol
logic in isolation: it never spawns grok, by design, because CI has no binary,
no auth, and no subscription. That left the actual CLI contract (wire shapes that

second layer: an on-demand suite that drives the real binary end-to-end and reuses

pre-release gate); research/{subagents,image-generation}.md updated to ground

Fix ask_user_question (#12); restore Q&A on resume; harden cross-agent resume

Grok's ask_user_question tool was broken end-to-end: the catch-all ACKed the
x.ai/ask_user_question server request with `{}`, which Grok's deserializer
rejects (internally-tagged enum needs an `outcome`), so every question failed
and Grok dumped it as plain text. Implement the real response contract
(recovered from the grok.exe binary, documented in research/ask-user-question.md)
plus an inline question card that confirms the choice clearly, restores
answered questions on session resume across both agent schemas (grok-build's
`ask_user_question` and the cursor/composer agent's `AskQuestion`, including the
replayed "Ask: <q>"-titled snapshots), and keeps a session's own model on resume
instead of crashing when the default model belongs to a different agent. v1.3.1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add voice input (v1.3.0): streaming dictation with hands-free "grok send"

Lets users dictate prompts via a composer mic button. Built deliberately
*outside* ACP because the grok CLI advertises promptCapabilities.audio:false
and rejects audio content blocks, and VS Code webviews can't reach the mic — so
capture runs in the extension host (an ffmpeg child process, like the CLI and
terminals) and transcription goes straight to xAI's separate Speech-to-Text
product (api.x.ai/v1/stt). Full feasibility write-up in research/voice-input.md.

- Live/streaming by default: ffmpeg PCM -> ws -> wss://api.x.ai/v1/stt, partial
  events accumulated by `start` (the trailing transcript.done is often empty as
  smart-turn finalizes mid-stream). grok.voiceStreaming:false falls back to the
  batch REST endpoint.
- Continuous + hands-free: saying "grok send" submits and restarts a fresh
  stream so the mic keeps listening (each message = one clean utterance);
  messages dictated while Grok is responding are queued and flushed when the
  turn ends, so you never touch the mouse/keyboard after the first click.
- "connecting -> listening" loading state so the first words aren't clipped;
  "grok send" highlighted in the composer; send/sent mishearing tolerated and
  the phrase passed as a `keyterm` bias; trailing punctuation kept and never
  doubled; listening is scoped to the active session (switch/resume/restart
  stops the mic).
